title: Error
description: The base shape of every non-zero exit under --json (DESIGN.md §3). A move the diagram doesn't draw adds allowed. A gate's refusal, from start, submit or the gates dry run, adds id, status, result, gates and failures, and exits 2.

error.description: One line saying what went wrong and how to fix it.

exit_code.description: The same as the process's exit code: 1 bad input, 2 refused by a gate, 3 the store, a file or git can't be read.

allowed.description: Only when a move was refused because the state diagram (DESIGN.md §2.2) doesn't draw it: every move allowed from the item's state, in the diagram's order. One entry per arrow in the diagram, so a command with two outcomes, such as submit from in-progress once triggers exist (slice 9), is listed once for each, with the same command. Empty for an item in review.

via.description: The command that makes the move.

to.description: The state the move leads to.

command.description: How to run it on this item, with … where a reason goes.

id.description: Only for a gate's refusal: the item's ID.

status.description: Only for a gate's refusal: the item's state. Only an in-progress item can be submitted, so for the gates dry run, an item in any other state would still be refused once every reason is fixed.

result.description: Only for a gate's refusal. For the gates dry run, it means a submit would be refused now.

gates.description: Only for a gate's refusal: every gate that ran, in order, with whether it passed.

secs.description: For G3 and G4, which run checks: how long their checks took together, in seconds.

failures.description: Only for a gate's refusal: every reason a gate failed, each with its gate, the criterion it's about if it's about one, numbered from 1, and a message saying what to do. A check that failed (G3 or G4) adds cmd, exit_code, timed_out and output.

cmd.description: For a check that failed: its command, a line of sh run in the project's root.

exit_code.description: For a check that failed: its exit code, or null if it was stopped, ran out of time, or couldn't be run.

timed_out.description: For a check that failed: whether it ran longer than the project's check_timeout_secs, and was stopped.

output.description: For a check that failed: its last 20 lines of output, stdout and stderr together, without a final line break. Each kept line is cut at 500 characters, the last of them `…`, if it's longer. Empty if it printed nothing.
